title: Explain a pull request
summary: A pull request, often called a PR, proposes combining changes from one branch into another. Its description should explain the result for a reviewer.
introduction: A pull request, often called a PR, proposes combining changes from one branch into another. Its description should explain the result for a reviewer. We will use a small example so you can follow each step.
learningObjectives: Use the example to answer a practice question

blocks.text: A pull request, often called a PR, proposes combining changes from one branch into another. Its description should explain the result for a reviewer.

blocks.code:

Problem: lowercase queries missed titles
Change: compare title and query in lowercase
Check: Moon and moon both match
blocks.title: Explain a pull request

blocks.text: The base receives the proposed changes. The head holds the change being reviewed. The explanation links the edit to a visible behaviour.

items: Read the example from top to bottom. Point to the part that uses the new idea.
Write a one-sentence PR description for a spelling correction.
Explain what changed in your own words. Check the example again if you get stuck.

blocks.title: A common mistake
blocks.text: Opening a PR does not mean it has been approved or merged.
For more detail later, use this [GitHub further reading](https://docs.github.com/en/get-started).
